title: Buying Redwood Inference via Cloud Marketplaces (AWS/GCP) — Internal Deck Outline (Sales/SE)
author: Soojin Lee
body:
## Purpose
This page is the source-of-truth outline for the internal Sales/SE deck used to guide buyers who prefer purchasing Redwood Inference via AWS Marketplace or Google Cloud Marketplace. It covers:
- How cloud marketplace procurement works (in practical terms)
- Which Redwood SKUs to recommend and how to position them
- Common objections and how to handle them
- A repeatable demo + onboarding flow for marketplace buyers

**Primary audience:** AEs, SEs, CS (procurement-stage support)

---

## When to use this deck
Use this deck when:
- The buyer explicitly says they must buy through AWS/GCP Marketplace to draw down cloud commit
- Procurement requests marketplace listing links, SKU names, or a purchase flow overview
- The buyer wants a PO/invoice through their cloud provider instead of direct contract billing

Do not use this deck as a general product pitch; pair it with the core Redwood platform deck.

---

## Speaker notes conventions
- **Slide content:** what appears on the slide
- **Talk track:** what the presenter says
- **Do/Don’t:** guardrails for claims (esp. security/compliance)

---

## Deck outline (recommended 12–16 slides)

### Slide 1 — Title: “Buying Redwood via Cloud Marketplaces (AWS/GCP)”
**Slide content**
- For enterprise procurement + faster activation
- Covers SKUs, purchase flow, onboarding, and FAQs

**Talk track**
- “We’ll make marketplace procurement predictable: which SKU to pick, what procurement needs, and how to get you live quickly.”

---

### Slide 2 — Why Marketplace: the 3 reasons buyers choose it
**Slide content**
- Draw down cloud commit (committed spend)
- Vendor onboarding simplification (security + legal)
- Consolidated invoicing through AWS/GCP

**Talk track**
- Reinforce that marketplace is a procurement channel; product experience remains Redwood.

---

### Slide 3 — Redwood deployment options (and how marketplace fits)
**Slide content**
- Hosted API (fastest time-to-value)
- Dedicated capacity (predictable throughput, isolation)
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem options)
- Marketplace purchase can map to: Hosted, Dedicated, and Private entitlements (depending on SKU)

**Talk track**
- “Marketplace is how you buy; Redwood Console is how you operate.”

---

### Slide 4 — How the procurement mechanics work (plain English)
**Slide content**
- Buyer purchases Redwood SKU in AWS/GCP Marketplace
- Cloud provider generates an entitlement (subscription record)
- Redwood receives entitlement event and activates matching features/capacity
- Buyer links the purchase to a Redwood org in Console

**Talk track**
- Set expectations: entitlement activation is typically fast, but sometimes delayed by marketplace systems; we monitor and have an escalation path.

---

### Slide 5 — Buyer journey: Purchase → Provision → First value
**Slide content**
1) Select SKU + region
2) Purchase/subscribe in Marketplace
3) Link entitlement to Redwood org (Console)
4) Validate activation
5) Run first inference call / deploy first endpoint

**Talk track**
- “We recommend a 10–15 minute ‘activation session’ with SE for first-time marketplace buyers.”

---

### Slide 6 — SKU taxonomy (what we sell on marketplaces)
**Slide content**
- **Hosted API**: usage-based, PLG-friendly
- **Dedicated**: reserved capacity (predictable throughput)
- **Private**: VPC/on-prem oriented packaging (enterprise controls)
- Add-ons (where applicable): compliance package, extended retention, premium SLA

**Talk track**
- Keep it simple: anchor on the deployment mode first, then add-ons.

**Do/Don’t**
- Don’t invent SKU names or promise custom line items beyond what’s listed.
- Do reference the latest SKU catalog page for exact naming.

---

### Slide 7 — SKU selection guide (decision tree)
**Slide content**
- Choose **Hosted API** if: fastest start, variable workloads, minimal infra involvement
- Choose **Dedicated** if: predictable high TPS, lower variance, data isolation, performance SLOs
- Choose **Private** if: regulated workloads, VPC/on-prem, customer-managed networking/KMS requirements

**Talk track**
- “We can start with Hosted for evaluation, then migrate to Dedicated or Private with consistent API patterns.”

---

### Slide 8 — Packaging guidance by persona
**Slide content**
- **Engineering lead:** latency, throughput, regions, reliability
- **Security/GRC:** encryption, audit logs, retention, access control, shared responsibility
- **Procurement/Finance:** invoicing, commit drawdown, upgrades, renewal

**Talk track**
- “Marketplace unblocks procurement; our operational story (SLOs, observability, rollouts) is what keeps teams live.”

---

### Slide 9 — Marketplace vs direct contract: when to recommend which
**Slide content**
Recommend **Marketplace** when:
- Must apply cloud commit
- Procurement prefers cloud vendor paper
- Faster PO/invoicing path

Recommend **Direct contract** when:
- Non-standard commercial terms are required
- Buyer needs bundles not supported as marketplace SKUs
- Complex multi-year enterprise agreement with custom clauses

**Talk track**
- “We can support either; we’ll choose the path that reduces cycle time and matches your internal requirements.”

---

### Slide 10 — Common objections (and how to respond)
**Slide content**
1) “Marketplace is slow / we’ll get stuck.”
2) “How do upgrades/downgrades work?”
3) “Can we get a private offer?”
4) “Will we still get enterprise support/SLA?”
5) “What about data residency and audit logs?”

**Talk track (soundbites)**
- **Slow/stuck:** “We’ve instrumented entitlement activation and have an internal escalation path; we’ll schedule an activation session.”
- **Upgrades/downgrades:** “We support plan transitions; we’ll coordinate the timing so entitlements and billing remain consistent.”
- **Private offer:** “Possible depending on marketplace; we’ll confirm with Partnerships/Finance.”
- **Support/SLA:** “Support routes the same; the SLA depends on the purchased SKU/add-on.”
- **Security/residency:** “We can share the marketplace security FAQ and the security packet under the appropriate terms.”

---

### Slide 11 — Security & compliance talk track (approved claims only)
**Slide content**
- Encryption in transit and at rest
- Audit logging availability (control plane events)
- SSO/SAML support (where applicable)
- Data retention and configurable retention add-ons (where applicable)
- Shared responsibility model: marketplace purchase ≠ buyer-managed deployment unless Private/on-prem

**Talk track**
- “We’ll provide clear documentation on what is configurable vs default. We avoid over-promising and stick to verified controls.”

**Do/Don’t**
- Don’t claim “HIPAA compliant” / “FedRAMP authorized” unless explicitly approved and current.
- Do offer: security FAQ + evidence index process (SOC 2 report under NDA where required).

---

### Slide 12 — Live demo flow (15–20 minutes)
**Slide content**
1) Show marketplace listing (SKU selection + region)
2) Explain purchase step (what the buyer will see)
3) Switch to Redwood Console: “Link Marketplace Purchase”
4) Show entitlement status + confirmation
5) Run “hello world” inference call (streaming)
6) Show usage/cost dashboard + audit trail entry

**Talk track**
- Highlight the exact screens buyers will use.
- Emphasize what to do if entitlement is “pending.”

---

### Slide 13 — What we need from the customer (checklist)
**Slide content**
- Cloud account ID / org owner email
- Intended region(s)
- Deployment mode target: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
- If Dedicated/Private: expected throughput, latency targets, and rollout timeline
- Security review needs: SOC 2 request path, encryption/KMS requirements, logging/retention requirements

**Talk track**
- “If we collect this up front, we reduce activation time and avoid org-linking issues.”

---

### Slide 14 — Operational expectations (SLOs + support)
**Slide content**
- Entitlement activation: typically minutes; escalations if delayed
- Support: standard channels; prioritize marketplace onboarding incidents
- Monitoring: Redwood tracks entitlement lag + provisioning errors

**Talk track**
- “We treat marketplace onboarding as a production pipeline with alerts and runbooks.”

---

### Slide 15 — Troubleshooting highlights (for SEs + CS)
**Slide content**
- Entitlement not visible yet → wait window + confirm correct account/region
- Linked to wrong Redwood org → remediation steps + prevention best practices
- Region mismatch (common in GCP) → supported region check + re-link steps
- Webhook delays → internal escalation to SRE/on-call + Partnerships

**Talk track**
- “We’ll guide the customer with a minimal set of steps, then take it offline quickly if it’s a back-end entitlement issue.”

---

### Slide 16 — Close: Next steps + mutual action plan (MAP)
**Slide content**
- Confirm desired SKU(s) + region
- Security packet request (if needed)
- Schedule 30-min activation session
- Define success criteria: first call, first workload, production go-live

**Talk track**
- “Procurement doesn’t have to slow the technical path—we’ll run both tracks in parallel.”

---

## Appendix slides (optional)

### Appendix A — AWS vs GCP differences (what to mention)
- Listing formatting and validation steps differ
- GCP region mismatches are more common; set expectations
- Private offer/discount mechanisms differ by marketplace

### Appendix B — SKU FAQ (internal)
- Which SKU for POC vs production
- How add-ons are represented (separate line items vs bundled)
- How renewals work in marketplace vs direct

### Appendix C — Email templates (AE/SE)
- “Here is the marketplace listing + what to purchase”
- “Here is what we need from you to activate”
- “Your entitlement is pending; here is what happens next”

---

## Internal call-to-action (maintenance)
